scope: Complete author reading of the glossary, all four Pattern pages and all five How-to pages, reconciled with existing domain-template, TypeScript, durable history, approval, external-effect and outbox execution evidence. This does not certify the defective historical multitenant example, a real external provider, remote outbox delivery or the known generated TypeScript output.

reviews.reason: Distinguishes the named application, task, durable, MCP and experimental terms and no longer implies that Aksara ships an autonomous multi-step Agent runtime.
Separates domain demonstrations from the tested Ticket Desk and describes basic versus flat template structure and authorization ownership.
Accurately describes the Post/Comment example, flat setup and denied unauthenticated seed path while requiring explicit custom-action authorization.
Matches Customer/Deal/Activity source and startup behavior and avoids presenting pipeline calculations as prediction, accounting or tenant security.
Keeps EX-001 and MIGRATION-001 visible, limits execution to inspection and routes production isolation work to the tested tenant tutorial.
Uses public service methods and states ordering, limit, non-snapshot, retired-action and retention boundaries without promising an event-sourced compliance ledger.
Separates reviewer and requester authorization, server-owned references, approval intent, expiry/conflict outcomes and later worker reauthorization.
Uses effect classes, stable downstream keys and reconciliation honestly and leaves provider idempotency, timeouts and delivery guarantees to the integration.
Matches claim, sink and acknowledgement transactions, duplicate-delivery risk, tenant selection and application-owned retention/observability.
Shows explicit generation while preserving the TypeScript 5.9.3 compile failure, import-discovery limitation and client authentication/error-handling responsibilities.

contradictions.boundary: The glossary defined Agent as a multi-step tool executor despite the linked page and stable contract excluding an autonomous Agent runtime.
contradictions.disposition: Agent now means a machine actor at the application boundary; experimental prompt/workflow helpers and autonomous runtime scope are stated separately.
